source.title: Covert Influence Between Language Models
source.authors: Avidan Shah; J. Chooi; Jinghuai Ou; Shi Feng

page_placements.theme: Phantom transfer: filtered natural-language outputs carry traits across base models
Prompt-only and in-context analogues beyond linked tokens
Teacher as scorer or logit source: on-policy and logit distillation transmit traits

record.tranche_reason: The paper reuses the number-carrier SFT setup and payload-expression evaluation associated with the original subliminal-learning claim, while adding carrier-selection conditions and cross-model tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SFT transfer experiments on number and filtered natural-language carriers, plus OPD and in-context transfer experiments. Rows for SFT results are often qualitative descriptions of figures because the text does not provide their numeric values. Cited findings from other papers are not recorded as results. The stealth-priming system-prompt result is recorded as a related but distinct prompt-only finding; it does not test insertion of linked tokens.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1 reuses the number-carrier SFT setup of Cloud et al. on Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, with 19 animals, an unconditioned-teacher control and random/top/bottom splits. It also reports a cross-size number-carrier test (Qwen 2.5 7B to 3B). These results bear directly on A and B, and the MDCL-vs-PVP contrast on numbers bears on D. The natural-language, OPD, in-context and stealth-priming experiments do not test any version as worded. Natural-language carriers are not semantically unrelated outputs; the authors argue this is a distinct phenomenon.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that covert influence is achievable through SFT, OPD and ICL, and that attribution-based selection is an upper-bound stress test. Number-carrier subliminal learning is less human-detectable and less portable. Natural-language transfer is portable and PVP-predictable, so they class it as a distinct semantic phenomenon. The 'less portable across model families' claim rests on one Qwen 7B→3B same-family pair.
record.recipe_differences: The SFT number-carrier setup follows the subliminal-learning setup with similar hyperparameters and evaluation infrastructure, but ranks data by MDCL or PVP and tests extra carrier types and model pairings. The paper also adds OPD and in-context interfaces.
record.method_sensitivity: SFT transfer depends on carrier type and selection method: MDCL selection amplifies number and natural-language transfer, while PVP predicts natural-language but not number transfer. Cross-model number transfer was not activated in the tested Qwen 2.5 7B-to-3B pairing; cross-model natural-language transfer was observed. In the in-context experiments, top versus bottom MDCL/PVP selection changes misalignment transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: Natural-language Alpaca completions, filtered three times for explicit mentions, transfer animal/entity payloads. This holds same-model (Qwen, Gemma, OLMo) and cross-model (Qwen 7B→3B, Gemma→OLMo). Transfer is predicted by both MDCL and persona-vector projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Filtered natural-language outputs carry a semantic, persona-level signal ('subtle generalization'/phantom transfer). It transfers across base models, unlike number-carrier subliminal learning.

fits_no_version.finding: On-policy distillation with target-script tokens masked from the sender still transfers a language-switching payload. Controls are 0%, and transfer also works cross-size within a family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: OPD can covertly transmit a behavioural disposition through the teacher's distribution over non-payload tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: In-context examples that pass an oracle monitor, written by a sender told to embed a risky persona covertly, raise broad emergent-misalignment rates in Gemini receivers (4.6%–11.8% vs near-zero).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Covertly constructed in-context demonstrations can induce broad emergent misalignment without fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Audit-clean generated system-prompt suffixes raise disfavoured-option choice in Gemma 4 31B from 0.03 to 0.58 (oracle pick).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantically neutral-seeming system prompts can steer a model's binary choices without fine-tuning (stealth priming).

record.problems: Many SFT outcomes are only shown in figures, without numerical values in the text. The authors caution that the cross-model number result is a null result for one model pairing, not proof that cross-model number transfer is impossible. The main text and appendix give different OPD transfer values for the cited Qwen and Llama comparisons. The authors also describe the setup as an upper bound because models are given attribution-based sample selection unavailable to an unaided sender.
record.rows_left_out: No additional SFT outcome types left out. Per-animal breakdowns and training curves in Appendix A and B are not separately extracted where they repeat the main comparisons. Other stealth-priming selector comparisons and codeword-selection experiments are omitted because they do not test linked-token prompting or the SFT trait-transmission claim.

untested.parts: Code and maths-reasoning carriers. Only one same-model pair (Qwen 2.5 7B) with number carriers.
Cross-family number transfer (e.g. Gemma→Qwen) is not tested; only Qwen 2.5 7B→3B.
Untested as worded. Misalignment is only tested via in-context examples written by a sender instructed to encode the persona covertly, with no fine-tuning on unrelated outputs.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens, steering-vector injection and the gradient argument are not tested directly. Only per-sample MDCL versus persona-vector projection is compared.
Untested: no full fine-tuning, no LoRA-rank sweep (r=8 only), no evaluation-prompt robustness test.
Untested: no linked-token insertion in prompts.

missing.what: MDCL-selected natural-language cross-model transfer from a Gemma teacher to an OLMo student (entity payloads)
Same-model Gemma-3-12B and Llama-3.1-8B OPD configurations and Gemma-3-12B→4B cross-size cells
Per-animal number-carrier results naming which animals transfer (e.g. elephant, dog unlocked under top-MDCL)

record.verdict_notes: Results are mostly figure-only, with no numbers in the text for SFT. The reader linked rows using V1–V6 instead of A–F; corrected here. The C 'supports' label was dropped because the ICL route is not fine-tuning and the carriers were deliberately constructed by an instructed sender. The B 'challenges' label was dropped because the cross-model transfer used natural-language carriers, which the paper argues is a different phenomenon. A researcher could reasonably read those rows as limiting B's scope to number-like carriers. LoRA r=8, 3 epochs, 10k samples, 3 seeds.

versions.untested_parts: Numbers and filtered natural-language samples are tested; code and maths-reasoning carriers are not tested. The natural-language results are not the same non-semantic number-carrier setup.
The cross-model number test is Qwen 2.5 7B to Qwen 2.5 3B; it does not test every unrelated model family or initialization.
Misalignment is tested through in-context examples, not through SFT on number, code, or maths data.

The paper compares MDCL and persona-vector projections as indicators of signal in different carrier types. It does not directly test token entanglement, divergence tokens, a steering-vector mechanism, or a gradient-based mechanism.
No full-fine-tuning comparison, LoRA-rank sweep, or SFT evaluation-prompt robustness test is reported.
The prompt-only experiments use generated system-prompt suffixes or in-context examples, not insertion of linked tokens.
